canonical_order.predicate_position: Sentence-final (Main verb, copula, or predicative adjective always closes the clause)
canonical_order.modifier_rule: Modifiers strictly precede their heads (Adjectives precede nouns; adverbs precede verbs; relative clauses precede head nouns)

bunsetsu_chunks.definition: The minimal pronounceable phrasal unit in Japanese, composed of one content word (Jiritsugo) followed by zero or more clitic functional words (Fuzokugo: particles/auxiliaries).

example.sentence: 私は図書館で本を読む。

relative_clauses.rule: Relative clauses precede the noun they modify with NO relative pronouns (e.g. who, which, that).
relative_clauses.example: 昨日買った本 (The book that [I] bought yesterday)
relative_clauses.ga_no_conversion: In adnominal relative clauses, subject particle 'が' optionally converts to 'の' (私が書いた論文 -> 私の書いた論文)

topic_comment.distinction: Topic (は) establishes discourse frame; Comment makes an assertion about the topic.

classic_example.literal: As for the elephant, the trunk is long.
classic_example.analysis: 象は = Topic (not grammatical subject of 長い); 鼻が = Syntactic subject of predicate 長い.

word_order_flexibility.scrambling: Pre-verbal constituents can freely reorder (scramble) without changing propositional truth value because case particles uniquely designate grammatical roles.
permutations: 太郎が花子に本をあげた。 (Canonical SOV)
花子に太郎が本をあげた。 (Scrambled)
本を太郎が花子にあげた。 (Scrambled for topical emphasis)

sentence_types.declarative: Ends in shuushikei verb or copula (本を読む / 本です).
sentence_types.interrogative: Formed by adding sentence-final particle 'か' (or rising intonation) without subject-aux inversion (本を読みますか).
sentence_types.imperative: Formed via Meireikei (読め) or request auxiliary (読んでください).
sentence_types.exclamative: Marked via final particles (なんと美しいことか / すごいな).
